chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Hamza, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Shall I inform you of the worst of your men?' We said, 'Yes, O Rasool-Allah!' So he said: 'Among the worst of your men are the slanderer, the audacious, the obscene, the one who eats alone, the one who withholds his provision, the one who beats his slave, and the one who causes his dependents to seek shelter with others.'

key_terms.الضَّارِبَ عَبْدَهُ: The one who beats his slave
key_terms.الْبَهَّاتَ: The slanderer or one who spreads rumors
key_terms.الْمَانِعَ رِفْدَهُ: The one who withholds his provision/gifts
key_terms.الْمُلْجِئَ عِيَالَهُ إِلَى غَيْرِهِ: The one who causes his dependents to seek shelter with others

ai.seo_question: What are the characteristics of the worst men according to this hadith from Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) identifies the 'worst of men' (*asharr ar-rijal*) through a series of specific moral and social vices, emphasizing the degradation of character through arrogance and selfishness. The term *al-bahhat* refers to those who boast and show off, while *al-fahhash* denotes one who is obscene or vulgar in speech and conduct. This description serves as a practical guide for evaluating individual character within the Shia tradition, linking internal moral decay to external social burdens such as stinginess and harshness toward dependents.
